sections.value:
PASS WITH NOTES - performance/313, round 1

Head: 8dd610594a1194320106f15233242e8764870b35.
No performance blocker. BEFORE is measured below; AFTER remains owed after deployment. This is a performance verdict, not a claim that the dependency-free review worktree passes the full local ship gate.

Cost review

- The existing observer schedule remains nominally 600 ms, one loop per daemon, with MissedTickBehavior::Delay. There is no new timer, configuration switch, process-launch site, or per-tick per-pane launch.
- For N tracked panes, the old capture load was approximately N/0.6 per second. The new load is approximately (active + unsettled panes)/0.6 plus quiet, replayable panes/30. Unknown, PendingClear, cursor changes, tap bytes, and conflicting or uncertain gate evidence still capture on the next pass. At N=186, an entirely settled quiet cohort averages at most about 6.2 backstop captures/s, rather than 310 observer captures/s.
- That 6.2/s is a sustained quiet-cohort average, NOT a maximum for any one second or the fleet's total captures. Synchronized backstops can capture all 186 panes in one pass; an unreadable or active fleet can still reach the old capture rate. The physical detection bound is the 30 s threshold plus the next observation's scheduling/control-client latency; [30 s, 30.6 s) is the deterministic test's bound, not a hard deadline under host overload.
- Per-pane attach/marker/pane_pipe checks and the first tap drain remain every pass through the existing control client and in-process file IO. Replaying skips the capture, composer parsing and trailing drain. Repair and control-client recovery retain their existing, counted launch sites.
- Counters add two relaxed atomic operations per pass, one per replay, and two or three per successful capture. They allocate no counter storage per tick. The replay path itself is not allocation-free: it clones the remembered composer and gate content, compares them, and retains one extra composer string per tracked pane. Its work scales with composer bytes and still uses the existing mutexes. This does not negate the IO/parse cut, but only AFTER can establish net CPU savings.

Prime's three checks, read against this exact head

1. InteractionGate::permits_injection_fresh -> fresh_injection_verdict -> injection_observation still drains the live tap, lists the cursor and takes its OWN capture. The skip does not replace the admission capture. Owned pane submission also retains its deciding capture under ownership.
2. decide is the former observation decision body, extracted without changing its gate calls. Replays call it with tap_active=false; gate ageing and edit timestamps are evaluated on those same calls. Unknown/PendingClear cannot replay. The composer recognizer reads screen/cursor input, not elapsed time.
3. CAPTURE_BACKSTOP is 30 s, checked against the last actual recognized capture, never refreshed by replay. A silent screen change is eventually captured even when all replay guards otherwise hold. This backstop is a BRAKE on skipping, not a new injection-authorization policy. Existing destructive tap-retirement/sweep policy is unchanged.

Counter interpretation

passes includes failed passes; active_us measures elapsed wall time inside them, NOT process CPU. captures/capture_bytes count successful observer capture returns, including subsequently unrecognized captures; failed capture attempts and injection-owned captures are not counted. backstop is a subset of those successful captures for which the replay backstop alone forced capture. Independent relaxed loads are not an atomic multi-field snapshot; use interval deltas, allowing endpoint skew. fetch_add wraps modulo 2^64 rather than saturating, but this is not a credible daemon-lifetime overflow: even at the old approximately 2.9 MB/s, capture_bytes takes about 200,000 years to wrap.

LIVE BEFORE - November 21, 2026

The CPU/launch interval did not overlap the busy-polling machine sampler.

Separate just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json:
20.0 s; daemon PID 43526; machine 438.7 new PIDs/s; sampled 408.9/s; 98,236 polls. Attribution lower bounds: other 149.4/s, gone-before-seen 259.5/s; no daemon child was caught. That absence is NOT proof of zero daemon launches. Observed statusline runs 0.5/s; Claude display/stop hooks 0.3/1.0 per second. This is a machine-load receipt, not feature-attributed cost. Sampling ended at 18:36:17 UTC+10. The much higher host load and rates than the author's older control prohibit treating their CPU baseline as a matched comparison.

Evidence and limits

- just pr-freeze 313: FINAL, exit 0 at this head; all five checks successful, merge CLEAN, no migration. git diff --check origin/main...HEAD: exit 0; review worktree clean.
- CI run 44884185946 is successful and names this exact head. Successful rust-test job 136785776994 ran cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci: 2774 tests passed, six excluded by the nextest selection. Its uploaded artifact is ID 14699755702, selected by the successful job's upload receipt, not by name. Downloaded zip SHA-256 eca3d35068621e14ea252e77078d6d89ccb0cc79dabb43f5529fae90639cb17f matches that receipt. JUnit explicitly includes 18/18 observer tests and all six spawn-site tests without failures/errors.
- The new injection, twin-observer ageing, dead-tap backstop and activity/cursor tests all appear in that artifact. I read their assertions and the author's M1-M6 RED receipts in PR comment 7059426240; I did not independently mutate the read-only tree. Those receipts were made at 587fe438; the observer/interaction files are identical at the requested merge head.
- harness boot --json: advisory NOT-READY because local node_modules is absent. harness checks --quick --json: exit 1, eight dependency/tooling failures; heavy Rust/route/smoke stages skipped. C25 honored: no dependency symlink/install, no local build, no bounce, no source changes. The local quick gate is not claimed green.

AFTER owed

After deploying a commit containing this head, repeat the same separately sampled CPU/RSS/load/spawn protocol with pinned daemon PID/start/commit and comparable fleet activity/uptime. Take two data.pane_observer readings and publish captures/s, capture_bytes/s, skipped/s, backstop/s and active_us/pass. Observer counters exclude injection captures; do not claim total tmux capture volume or CPU attribution from those counters alone. No post-deploy saving is claimed in this verdict.

magicWand: one read-only live-cost receipt command that pins process identity, commit, per-instrument monotonic timestamps, load and counter definitions, and keeps the machine sampler separate from the CPU window.
difficulties: dependency-free reviews cannot reproduce the full local TS gate; observer-only counters and wall-time active_us are easy to overinterpret as total tmux work or CPU.
